title: Sprite/2D art ai animation tools?
author: Kimblethedwarf
selftext:
Genuine question. Whats our there for open source tools to help automate animation rigging? I've created sprites, even broken then down into into parts to properly rig together for movement. But for the life of my I cant animate them correctly, and they look like patched together peices of paper rather than a singular 2d sprite moving...

Any advice?

https://i.redd.it/0yvhiszlvm3i1.png

comments.author: teejayaiartdirector
comments.body: Go 100% procedural! 🔥 Seriously don't waste time on 2d sprites!

replies.author: Kimblethedwarf
replies.body: Could you elaborate? Im a newb

replies.author: teejayaiartdirector
replies.body: Get the AI to code the graphics, music and sound fx for you using code and math! There is no need for game assets anymore, you can still use images and videos as reference material doing procedural.

replies.author: Kimblethedwarf
replies.body:
Hmmm, I have, I've been having claude fable be my head/lead and then codex delegated for art and other agents to critique and keep style in check for image generation.

I'm having a hard time getting the animations right. I have a cool pose of a solider in battle stance, but getting that image to then stand idle, fire, run, fall over, etc it just broke up the sprite and made funny walking men lol. 

Any tips or pointers would be appreciated.

replies.author: teejayaiartdirector
replies.body: I don't think you understand what I'm saying, you don't do image generation. You just skip it entirely or you just use the image for reference! Give the AI the image as reference and ask it to make that image for you procedural using code and math and ask it to animate it, animation with procedural is great!

replies.author: Kimblethedwarf
replies.body:
Hmmm, I dont think I do. I've tried asking it to do this a few different ways and have very failed results each time. 

I know people are a bit hush hush about how we prompt and get good results, but would love to understand exactly how you are getting decent results.

Would be happy to PM you.

replies.author: Kimblethedwarf
replies.body:
well fuck... its not quite as clean as my original art.. but with some tweaks.. fuck that is so much nicer and the animations more believable....

Cheers!

replies.author: Post-reality
replies.body: Dude, that's a bad advice. If he wants low quality then go ahead, but high quality ones require specifc diffusion and audio models, not coding agents.

comments.author: StainlessRocket
comments.body: Aesprite? Pixel lab? Or get the 3D animation  Claude code can use for 2d
